newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast power flat on mild temps, unit return.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast power flat on mild temps, unit return.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast ended Thursday mostly flat versus Tuesday's levels on mild temperatures and return of a large nuclear power unit to full operation.
"The loads are way off because of the weather," a New York trader said.

The latest weather forecast showed most of the Northeast would stay well above normal through the weekend with Friday readings peaking in 30-40 Fahrenheit degree range and bottoming in the teens to the 30s. Northern Maine could experience minimum temperatures in the single digits and maximum temperatures in the 20s.

The 1,137 megawatt Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear unit resumed full power output after being shut a week ago for repairs, Bulk power business in the region was light with many participants still absent due to the Christmas holiday, market sources said.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices for Friday delivery in the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) held at $20.00-$22.00 a megawatt hour (MWh).
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in western NYPP remained in a notational range of $14.00-$15.00, off from Tuesday's $15.00-$16.00 for Thursday.
In eastern NYPP, Friday's peak, non-firm power was still pegged at $26.50-$28.00/MWh.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Friday stayed at $18.00-$19.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Friday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border were held at $30.00-$33.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Friday delivery to the NU border was still assessed at $20.00-$22.00.
